logical_component_title: RiskPilot Data Lifecycle: Backup, Restore, and Threat Data Oversight

vulnerabilities.title: Sensitive data exposure in backups (backup/restore pipeline)
vulnerabilities.description: Backups copy and persist sensitive domain data, including user passwords, verification codes, and JSON fields containing heat maps, compliance and OWASP data. The backup SQLite database is not encrypted, and backups may be stored with broad access, increasing the risk of exfiltration or leakage.

compliance_controls.ISO27001_A11_PHYSICAL_SECURITY: ISO 27001 - A.11 Physical and Environmental Security

vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Do not export or expose highly sensitive fields (e.g., user.password, raw_scan_data) in backups. Encrypt backups at rest (e.g., with AES-256-GCM or a cloud KMS-managed key) and store encryption keys separately with strict access controls. Redact or tokenize sensitive fields in the backup payload. Enforce access control and audit trails for backup/restore operations. Implement integrity verification (checksums/digital signatures) for backup archives.
vulnerabilities.location: backup.py (create_backup, restore_backup) – fields copied include User.password, heat_map_data, compliance_tracker_data, OWASP_tracker_data, raw_scan_data
vulnerabilities.snippet: downloaded_user = User(id=..., password=..., ...); downloaded_verification_code = VerificationCode(..., code=...); ...; all_llm_scans = session.exec(select(LLMScan)).all() ...

vulnerabilities.title: Lack of encryption and hard-coded backup path (Windows path)
vulnerabilities.description: Backups are written to and read from a hard-coded, Windows-style path and the database file is a plain SQLite file. There is no encryption or key management of the backup data.

owasp_top_10.SOFTWARE_AND_DATA_INTEGRITY_FAILURES: A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures

vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Make backup path configurable and cross-platform using Path(). Use a secure, encrypted storage format (encrypted SQLite DB or encrypted container/file) with strict access controls. Do not rely on hard-coded file names or user-writable locations. Rotate and protect encryption keys via a KMS or secure vault.
vulnerabilities.snippet: sqlite_file_name = "backups\\26-11-2025-at-10_37_09-AM-Backup.db"

vulnerabilities.title: Path traversal risk in file write (unvalidated path)
vulnerabilities.description: A path variable is used to write to a file with open(path, 'wb'), where path is derived from user input. This enables path traversal and arbitrary file writes outside the intended directory.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Validate and sanitize all file paths. Use a fixed base directory and resolve/validate against it (pathlib.Path with strict checks). Reject any path containing .. or absolute paths. Prefer a safe file storage API that enforces allowed directories.
vulnerabilities.snippet: with open(path, 'wb') as file:  # potential path traversal if path is untrusted

vulnerabilities.title: Potential data duplication/overwrite on restore (PK conflicts)
vulnerabilities.description: Restoration inserts records with explicit IDs into PostgreSQL without handling potential existing records. If records exist with the same IDs, this can raise IntegrityError or cause unintended overwrites.

compliance_controls.ISO27001_A6_ORGANIZATION_OF_INFORMATION_: ISO 27001 - A.6 Organization of Information Security

vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Wrap restoration in a transaction and implement idempotent upserts (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE or SQLModel.merge). Validate existence before insert. Consider a restore-mode flag to either skip existing records or perform updates.
vulnerabilities.location: backup.py: Restoring the data loop (for user, verification_code, etc.)
vulnerabilities.snippet: remote_session.add(new_user); remote_session.commit()  # potential duplicate key error; consider merge/upsert

vulnerabilities.title: No auditing or authorization checks for backup/restore operations
vulnerabilities.description: Backup/restore functions lack explicit access control and audit logging, increasing risk from misuse and complicating incident investigations.

owasp_top_10.SECURITY_LOGGING_AND_MONITORING_FAILURES: A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Require authenticated admin authorization for backup/restore. Add structured audit logs with operator identity, timestamp, action, and record counts. Consider using a dedicated backup service with access controls.
vulnerabilities.snippet: def create_backup(...): ...    # ensure caller has admin rights and log action

vulnerabilities.title: No data integrity verification for backups
vulnerabilities.description: Backups are created and restored without integrity checks, making tampering or data corruption easier to miss.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Compute and store per-backup hashes or a signed manifest. Validate integrity on restore. Consider digital signatures and separate storage of the verification data.
vulnerabilities.snippet: # after writing backup, compute hash; verify before restore

logical_component_title: JWT-based Authentication, Password Handling, and Token Lifecycle

vulnerabilities.title: Path Traversal in file upload/write logic
vulnerabilities.description: The application writes uploaded or derived file paths directly to disk using a path assembled from potentially untrusted input (e.g., image_file/unique_path derived values) and opens it with open(path, 'wb'). Without strict validation or isolation to a designated uploads directory, an attacker can manipulate the path to access or overwrite arbitrary files outside the intended directory.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Validate and sanitize all user-controlled file paths. Do not construct filesystem paths from client input. Use a fixed uploads directory and sanitize file names (e.g., strip path separators, enforce allowed extensions). Consider using a safe file storage approach (e.g., Starlette's UploadFile) and os.path.normpath with a whitelist check to ensure the final path resides within the designated uploads directory. Remove any path traversal patterns (../, ..\) before writing. Consider using a library like werkzeug's secure_filename or equivalent.
vulnerabilities.location: backend/api_routes/routing_normal_sys.py around the file write operation (e.g., line where: with open(path, 'wb') as file:).
vulnerabilities.snippet:
with open(path, "wb") as file:
    ...

vulnerabilities.title: Missing audience/issuer validation and clock-skew handling in JWT usage
vulnerabilities.description: JWTs are created with HS256 and separate secrets for access/refresh. The code paths shown rely on token verification without explicit validation of audience (aud) or issuer (iss), and without mitigating clock skew (exp). This can lead to tokens being accepted outside intended audience boundaries or failing under small clock drifts between systems.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: When decoding/validating tokens, require and verify claims such as iss and aud, and enforce exp with an acceptable leeway (clock skew). If using jose/jwt libraries, explicitly set issuer/audience checks and consider using RS256 with rotation instead of a symmetric HS256 key for stronger key management. Centralize token validation logic and reject tokens with invalid/absent claims.
vulnerabilities.snippet:
decoded = jwt.decode(token, JWT_SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[ALGORITHM], audience=EXPECTED_AUDIENCE, issuer=EXPECTED_ISSUER)
# or equivalent verification that enforces iss/aud and applies a clock skew leeway

vulnerabilities.title: No refresh token rotation/revocation mechanism
vulnerabilities.description: Refresh tokens are issued and used to obtain new access tokens, but there is no rotation or revocation of used refresh tokens. If a refresh token is compromised, an attacker can continue to obtain new access tokens until the refresh token expires.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Implement refresh token rotation: store a hash of refresh tokens in the DB, invalidate the current token once used, and issue a new refresh token with each refresh request. Consider revoking tokens on logout and short-lived refresh tokens with aud/iss checks. Add server-side revocation lists or token blacklisting as needed.
vulnerabilities.location: backend/routing_auth.py in refresh endpoint and get_current_user_from_refresh_token / token persistence layer.
vulnerabilities.snippet:
async def refresh(data: RefreshToken, ...):
    user = await get_current_user_from_refresh_token(engine, data.refresh_token)
    # on success, issue new access_token and a new refresh_token, invalidating the old refresh token

vulnerabilities.title: Unvalidated Authorization header parsing and potential crash
vulnerabilities.description: get_user endpoint parses the Authorization header via Authorization.split(" ")[1] without validating the header structure. If the header is missing or not in the expected 'Bearer <token>' format, this can raise exceptions or lead to improper handling of authentication.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Parse and validate the Authorization header using a proper security dependency (e.g., FastAPI's OAuth2PasswordBearer or HTTPBearer) and return 401/400 for missing or malformed headers. Do not manually split without checks; handle exceptions gracefully and avoid leaking stack traces or sensitive data.
vulnerabilities.snippet:
auth_header = Authorization or ''
if not auth_header.startswith('Bearer '):
    raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail='Invalid authorization header')
token = auth_header.split(' ')[1]

vulnerabilities.title: Weak password policy on signup
vulnerabilities.description: Signup enforces a relatively weak password minimum (min_length=5, max_length=24). This may lead to weak credentials being created if clients do not enforce stronger local policies or if password entropy is insufficient.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Increase minimum password length (e.g., 12+), enforce complexity requirements (uppercase, lowercase, digits, special chars), and consider password strength estimation. Provide user feedback on password strength and server-side validation for all signup inputs.
vulnerabilities.snippet:
class UserSignup(BaseModel):
    password: str = Field(..., min_length=12, description='user password')

vulnerabilities.title: Verbose logging of PII and potentially sensitive data
vulnerabilities.description: Code paths log user emails and other details (e.g., 'user.email', error traces). In production, this can lead to exposure of PII in logs, especially if logs are not properly protected or rotated.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Use structured logging with redaction for PII, set appropriate log levels, and avoid printing full emails or tokens. Consider centralized logging with access controls and ensure logs do not contain sensitive tokens or secrets.
vulnerabilities.location: Multiple spots in routing_auth.py and related modules (e.g., login(), send_verification_code, error handlers).
vulnerabilities.snippet: print(f'user {user.email} logged in...')  # replace with redacted logging

logical_component_title: JWT-based Access/Refresh Token Authentication and Session Validation

vulnerabilities.title: Refresh token exception path uses potentially uninitialized token_data and revokes session on decode/validation errors
vulnerabilities.description: In get_current_user_from_refresh_token, the code entrypoint decodes the refresh token inside a try block and then, in the exception handler, references token_data.sub to look up the user and revoke the session. If the decode/validation fails, token_data may not be defined, leading to a NameError. Additionally, the exception path revokes the user session even when the user cannot be identified, which can cause unintended session revocation and instability.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Do not reference token_data in the exception path unless it is guaranteed to exist. Decode the token inside a try/except and, on failure, attempt to extract the subject from the raw payload if possible, or simply return an HTTP 401/403 without mutating user state. If revocation is required, only revoke after confirming a valid subject and user exists. Example fix: separate the decoding/validation path from revocation logic, guard all accesses with None checks, and avoid touching database when the token cannot be decoded. Also ensure token_data is defined before use and handle the case where the user record does not exist.
vulnerabilities.snippet:
except(jwt.JWTError, ValidationError):
    with Session(engine) as session:
        statement = select(User).where(User.email == token_data.sub)
        user = session.exec(statement).first()
        user.session_active = False
        session.add(user)
        session.commit()
        print(f"User {user.email} session deactivated {datetime.now(timezone.utc)} 🔴")
    raise HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
        detail="Could not validate credentials",
        headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
    )

vulnerabilities.title: Access token expiry checks use naive datetime comparisons, risking incorrect expiry validation
vulnerabilities.description: The code compares token_data.exp using datetime.fromtimestamp(...) without timezone awareness, and compares against datetime.now() (naive). This can cause incorrect expiry validation on systems with different timezones or clock skew, potentially granting access with expired tokens or denying valid tokens.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Use UTC-aware datetimes for expiry checks. Convert exp to a timezone-aware datetime and compare against datetime.now(timezone.utc). Ensure TokenPayload.exp is a numeric epoch (seconds) and use: if datetime.fromtimestamp(token_data.exp, timezone.utc) < datetime.now(timezone.utc): ...
vulnerabilities.snippet:
if datetime.fromtimestamp(token_data.exp) < datetime.now():
    print("Token expired 🔴")
    raise HTTPException(
        status_code = status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
        detail="Token expired",
        headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
    )

vulnerabilities.title: Missing issuer (iss) and audience (aud) validation in JWT processing
vulnerabilities.description: JWTs are decoded without validating issuer/audience claims. This opens the door for tokens from other sources or tampered tokens to be accepted if they are structurally valid and signed with the expected key. Lack of iss/aud reduces token integrity guarantees.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Validate issuer and audience during JWT decoding. Include iss and aud in the token payload and verify them in jwt.decode (e.g., jwt.decode(token, JWT_SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[ALGORITHM], issuer='your-issuer', audience='your-audience')). Store the expected issuer/audience in config and rotate as needed.
vulnerabilities.snippet:
payload = jwt.decode(token, JWT_SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[ALGORITHM], issuer='your-issuer', audience='your-audience')
token_data = TokenPayload(**payload)

vulnerabilities.title: Potential None dereference and unsafe session deactivation in refresh path
vulnerabilities.description: In exception handling branches of get_current_user_from_refresh_token, the code accesses user.email and deactivates the session without verifying that user is not None. If the user is not found, this dereference will raise an exception, potentially leaking information or causing server errors and undesired side effects.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: After querying the user, always check for None before dereferencing properties. Only revoke/modify the user state if a valid user object is retrieved. Example fix: if user is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail="Could not find user") else: user.session_active = False; ...
vulnerabilities.snippet:
with Session(engine) as session:
    statement = select(User).where(User.email == token_data.sub)
    user = session.exec(statement).first()
    if user is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail="Could not find user")
    user.session_active = False
    session.add(user)
    session.commit()
    print(f"User {user.email} session deactivated {datetime.now(timezone.utc)} 🔴")

logical_component_title: Verification Code Delivery, Password Reset, and Verification-Based Authentication Flows

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure storage of verification codes (plaintext)
vulnerabilities.description: Verification codes are stored in the VerificationCode table as plain text (field 'code'). If the database is leaked or misconfigured, OTPs can be exfiltrated and reused by an attacker to compromise user accounts. This also impedes ability to rotate or invalidate codes safely.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Hash the stored verification codes instead of persisting them in plaintext. Store a salted hash (e.g., bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2) and verify by hashing the provided code and comparing to the stored hash. Remove any plaintext code exposure in logs. Consider using a dedicated code verifier with a short TTL and rotation strategy.
vulnerabilities.snippet:
class VerificationCode(SQLModel,table=True):
    id : int | None = Field(default=None,primary_key=True)
    email : str
    code : str  # currently plaintext; should be hashed
    created_at : datetime.datetime | None= Field(default=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc),sa_type=DateTime)
    expires_at : datetime.datetime | None= Field(default=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) + datetime.timedelta(minutes=10),sa_type=DateTime)

vulnerabilities.title: Code expiry defaults misconfigured and expiry not enforced during verification
vulnerabilities.description: The VerificationCode model uses defaults that are evaluated at import time (created_at and expires_at) and do not represent per-record creation times. More critically, verification paths do not enforce expiry (expires_at is not consulted when validating a code). This allows use of codes long after issuance or after the TTL has passed, weakening OTP security.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Change created_at and expires_at to use default_factory to compute per-row values at insertion time. Enforce expiry in all verification checks by comparing now() with expires_at before accepting a code. On success, delete or invalidate the code.
vulnerabilities.location: backend/models.py - class VerificationCode; verification flow in routing_auth.py
vulnerabilities.snippet:
class VerificationCode(SQLModel,table=True):
    id : int | None = Field(default=None,primary_key=True)
    email : str
    code : str
    created_at : datetime.datetime | None= Field(default=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc),sa_type=DateTime)  # should be default_factory
    expires_at : datetime.datetime | None= Field(default=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) + datetime.timedelta(minutes=10),sa_type=DateTime)  # should be default_factory

vulnerabilities.title: Non-cryptographic randomness for verification codes
vulnerabilities.description: Verification codes are generated using Python's random module (random.choices). This is not cryptographically secure and may be predicted, increasing the risk of OTP brute-forcing or guessing.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Use a cryptographically secure RNG (e.g., secrets.randbelow/choices with a cryptographic RNG) to generate the 6-digit code. Ensure the code is zero-padded to 6 digits.
vulnerabilities.snippet:
def generate_verification_code():
    import random
    code = ''.join(random.choices('0123456789', k=6))
    return code  # Use secrets.choice or secrets.randbelow for crypto-security

vulnerabilities.title: Logging sensitive data and potential credential exposure
vulnerabilities.description: Error handling and logging occasionally print exception details that may include sensitive data (e.g., error objects, tokens, or graph credentials). This can leak secrets through logs, dashboards, or error reports.

owasp_top_10.SECURITY_LOGGING_AND_MONITORING_FAILURES: A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Avoid logging sensitive data. Implement structured logging with redaction for secrets and tokens. Use a centralized secret manager. Do not print or log exact exception contents that may reveal credentials.
vulnerabilities.location: backend/routing_auth.py - exception handlers (e.g., print(f"error in send_verification_code: {e} 🔴"))
vulnerabilities.snippet:
except Exception as e:
    print(f"error in send_verification_code: {e} 🔴")  # avoid logging sensitive data

vulnerabilities.title: Potential exposure of Graph/SMTP credentials and insecure transport considerations
vulnerabilities.description: Credential handling for external email delivery (Graph API credentials, SMTP) must avoid leakage in logs and ensure transport security. Hard-coding or logging credentials can lead to credential leakage and unauthorized access.

owasp_top_10.SECURITY_LOGGING_AND_MONITORING_FAILURES: A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Store Graph API credentials and SMTP secrets in a secret manager or environment with tight access controls. Rotate credentials regularly and ensure logs do not contain tokens or secret values. Prefer short-lived tokens and minimize logging of sensitive data.
vulnerabilities.location: backend/auth_utils.py / send_outlook_email implementation (Graph/SMTP integration) - credential handling
vulnerabilities.snippet: desired_secret_management_practice = os.environ.get('GRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET')  # should not be logged or printed

vulnerabilities.title: Default timestamps using function calls at import time (static values)
vulnerabilities.description: Using default values like Field(default=datetime.datetime.now(...)) leads to static values across records and can cause unexpected expiry behavior. This pattern is unsafe for time-sensitive data like OTPs.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Use default_factory for dynamic timestamps (created_at, expires_at) so each record gets a fresh timestamp. Example: created_at: Field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc)), expires_at: Field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(minutes=10)).
vulnerabilities.location: backend/models.py - VerificationCode model (created_at and expires_at fields)
vulnerabilities.snippet:
created_at : datetime.datetime | None = Field(default=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc), sa_type=DateTime)
expires_at : datetime.datetime | None = Field(default=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) + datetime.timedelta(minutes=10), sa_type=DateTime)
